jobs.title: Staff Pharmacist, Ohio
jobs.description_html:
Company Overview:

Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.  Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients. 

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock. 

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

Hours: Full-time, salaried (40hrs/week), Mon-Fri, 7:30am-9pm ET rotating shifts and rotating Saturdays 7:00am-5pm ET

The Opportunity:

As a BlinkRx Pharmacist, you are the clinical backbone of our closed-door facility. You will verify prescriptions with speed and precision, provide proactive phone-based patient counseling, and collaborate with prescribers to keep medications moving without compromising safety. This role is ideal for pharmacists who thrive in a structured, high-throughput environment and are passionate about improving patient outcomes at scale. 

Responsibilities:

Prescription Verification and Dispensing

  • Review and clinically verify new and refill prescriptions for therapeutic appropriateness, drug-drug interactions, contraindications, and dosing accuracy
  • Validate prescription data entry performed by pharmacy technicians, ensuring transcription accuracy from provider orders and transfer records
  • Perform pharmacist verification of filled prescriptions in a closed-door fulfillment environment, confirming accuracy of drug, dose, quantity, NDC, and labeling prior to release for shipment   
  • Perform daily prospective drug utilization review (DUR) to identify and resolve clinical flags before fulfillment
  • Manage specialty medication handling requirements including cold-chain verification

Patient Care

All patient interaction at BlinkRx is conducted by phone or digital platforms. Our pharmacists are the primary clinical contact for patients and must deliver a high standard of care in every call.

  • Provide proactive outbound patient counseling calls for new prescriptions, addressing drug education, expected side effects, dosing instructions, storage requirements, and adherence strategies
  • Handle inbound clinical patient calls related to counseling and clinical inquiries, while directing non-clinical inquiries, such as refill status and delivery questions, to the patient support team.
  • Document all patient interactions thoroughly in the patient profile within the pharmacy management system
  • Support Spanish-speaking patients with bilingual counseling where applicable

Prescriber Collaboration and Clinical Outreach

  • Contact prescriber offices via phone and electronic messaging to clarify incomplete, ambiguous, or clinically inappropriate prescriptions prior to dispensing
  • Partner with prescribers on therapeutic substitutions, DAW overrides, and formulary alternatives to reduce dispensing delays

Pharmacy Technician Supervision and Workflow Management

  • Supervise pharmacy technicians across data entry, prescription processing, packaging, and fulfillment workflows in accordance with state board regulations and in collaboration with technician management
  • Conduct real-time quality checks on technician work product, providing immediate corrective feedback to maintain accuracy standards
  • Identify and escalate technician performance trends to pharmacy leadership; participate in coaching and training as directed

Compliance, Safety and Quality

  • Ensure strict compliance with HIPAA, state pharmacy practice acts, federal DEA regulations, and all BlinkRx corporate policies
  • Oversee proper handling, documentation, and destruction of PHI-containing records and materials in alignment with privacy protocols
  • Participate in quality assurance activities including internal audits, prescription error tracking, and near-miss reporting
  • Report adverse drug events and medication errors through established pharmacovigilance channels, when applicable
  • Maintain fulfillment area compliance standards, including proper storage of temperature-sensitive medications

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with pharmacy leadership, patient services, clinical, compliance, and technology teams to drive operational and clinical improvements
  • Coordinate with the shipping and fulfillment team to resolve packaging errors, return-to-sender issues, and delivery failures affecting patient medication access
  • Provide clinical input on technology enhancements, workflow tools, and software configurations that affect the pharmacist verification or patient counseling experience
  • Participate in team huddles, quality reviews, and department meetings to support continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications:

Required

Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.  Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients. 

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock. 

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

Hours: Full-time, salaried (40hrs/week), Mon-Fri, 7:30am-9pm ET rotating shifts and rotating Saturdays 7:00am-5pm ET

  • Manage specialty medication handling requirements including cold-chain verification

  • Support Spanish-speaking patients with bilingual counseling where applicable

Responsibilities

  • Explains care plan options and the use, side effects, and contraindications of medications dispensed, either verbally and/or via written records, stored within proprietary software.

  • Ensures that patient care decisions and actions as well as coding/billing are properly documented using proprietary software system.

  • Ensures accurate, efficient, timely and compliant medication distribution and fulfillment for patients using proprietary software.

  • Plans, implements, and maintains procedures for assessing, compounding, packaging, and labeling medications, according to policy and legal requirements, to ensure quality, security, and proper disposal.

  • Oversee Pharmacy Technicians to ensure appropriate medication reconciliation, physician order entry, inventory management, medication storage and security conditions, and medication labelling and packaging as well as compliance to company policies and procedures and regulatory guidelines.

  • Provides timely review, preparation/compounding, and final approval for prescription orders and dispensed medications ensuring the correct drug, dosage form, directions, quantity, days’ supply, number of refills and packaging/labelling, including ancillary warnings, is entered into the appropriate patient profile, and dispensed to the correct patient. Works to ensure proper and compliant billing and record keeping of medications dispensed and shipped.

  • Uses professional judgment to provide timely, accurate and appropriate pharmaceutical care appropriately assessing new medication requests and refills making recommendations, in writing or via telephone to care providers to enhance patient outcomes and/or safety as needed in relation to care plans, changes, issues, and education.

  • Ensures compliance to state and federal laws and applicable rules and regulations as well as internal policies and procedures required for pharmacy practice. Reports and works to rectify or prevent any incidents of QAs, HIPAA violations, Fraud, Waste and Abuse or other problems or violations.

  • Embody AnewHealth’s Core Values in all communications and interactions.

  • This position may require weekend/on-call and holiday shifts.

jobs.description_html:
We’re hiring an Underwriter-Pharmacy in our Commercial Operations Division!

 

The Underwriter – Pharmacy is part of a team within Underwriting that works on all things pharmacy related: pricing, contracts, configuration, and more.  We evaluate critical information to assess risk and provide financial stability related to a client’s pharmacy claim costs, incorporating any known marketplace impacts within the analytics.  Pharmacy is a fast-paced, ever-changing environment, requiring critical thinking, flexibility, problem solving, accuracy, quality, and making sound underwriting decisions.

 

You’ll be successful in this role if you are a driven, adaptable self-starter who is very detail-oriented, excels at math, and able to comprehend complex information.  We are searching for someone who can balance detailed analysis with strategic thinking, as candidates must be comfortable both digging into underlying data and communicating findings at a high level.  Success in this position depends on strong organizational skills, the ability to manage multiple priorities, and a willingness to collaborate with cross-functional teams.  We foster a culture where innovation is encouraged.  That includes using AI enabled tools responsibly to support everyday work — guided by proven workflows, templates, and policies.

 

 Notes:

  • This remote position offers a Monday – Friday 8-hour work schedule primarily between the hours of 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. ET.

  • Corresponding with sales, account managers, agents, and other parties regarding group health insurance products, features, and pricing.

jobs.description_html:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

Job Description

Import/Export Coordinator – Malaysia


JOB DESCRIPTION

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life - enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while taking science a step beyond through research, development and delivery of life-changing therapies. With clinical trials conducted in 100+ countries and ongoing development of novel frameworks for clinical research through our PPD clinical research portfolio, our work spans laboratory, digital and decentralized clinical trial services. Your determination to deliver quality and accuracy will improve health outcomes that people and communities depend on – now and in the future.

IMPORT/EXPORT COORDINATOR

SUMMARIZED PURPOSE

Responsible and accountable for the planning and execution of moderate to complex Import & Export activities for assigned studies in Malaysia. Reviews, collects, and/or prepares documents for import license and regulatory submissions. Responsible for coordination of Import & Export transactions through delivery to depots/Site while ensuring compliance with company requirements and applicable regulations.

In addition to Import/Export Coordinator responsibilities, the role will also act as the Importer of Record (IoR) for assigned studies in Malaysia. The individual will support regulatory submissions, maintain regulatory documentation, interact with regulatory authorities, and ensure inspection and audit readiness in accordance with local regulatory requirements.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND OTHER JOB INFORMATION

Import/Export Coordinator Responsibilities
• Ensure that import & export activities are performed according to Thermo Fisher Scientific requirements, client requirements, and applicable regulations.
• Ensure an Import & Export plan is in place for each assigned project.
• Coordinate import & export transactions with customs brokers, freight forwarders, couriers, depots, and internal stakeholders.
• Actively problem solve and suggest solutions to import/export challenges.
• Maintain Import & Export files, metrics, and reports.
• Meet with management to discuss import & export issues and provide recommendations.
• Perform additional logistics and administrative activities according to business needs.
• Participate in ongoing training related to import/export regulations and GDP/GMP activities.

Importer of Record (IoR) Responsibilities
• Act as the designated Importer of Record (IoR) for assigned studies in Malaysia.
• Prepare, review, compile, and submit documentation required for import permit and regulatory applications.
• Liaise directly with the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) and other regulatory authorities as required.
• Attend regulatory meetings and support submission activities, including physical submissions when required.
• Maintain physical and electronic regulatory records in accordance with company procedures and regulatory requirements.
• Ensure documentation remains inspection- and audit-ready at all times.
• Travel to the office as required for document preparation, filing, record maintenance, and audit support activities.
• Support regulatory inspections and audits related to IoR activities.

JOB KNOWLEDGE
Applies acquired job skills and company policies and procedures to complete assigned tasks.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED
Normally follows established procedures on routine work and requires instructions only on new assignments.

BUSINESS RELATIONSHIPS
Contacts are typically with individuals within own department and frequently with external stakeholders including customs brokers, regulatory authorities, couriers, depots, and study teams.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required:
• Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) or equivalent Pharmacy degree.
• Registered Pharmacist with a valid Malaysian practicing license.
• Based in Kuala Lumpur or surrounding area with the ability to travel locally as required.

Preferred:
• Knowledge of Malaysian pharmaceutical import/export regulations.
• Experience in clinical supplies, logistics, regulatory affairs, import/export operations, or pharmaceutical environments.
• Familiarity with clinical supply terminology, practices, and principles.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

• Strong sense of ownership, accountability, and attention to detail.
• Maintains awareness of local regulatory changes concerning Import & Export activities.
• Daily interaction with customs brokers, forwarders, couriers, depots, and regulatory authorities.
• Ability to maintain confidential, accurate, and audit-ready documentation.
• Strong organizational and record management skills.
• Strong communication skills both written and verbal.
• Good level of English (verbal and written).
• Ability to work independently while effectively managing multiple priorities.
• Willingness to travel locally to NPRA and company offices as required.

jobs.title: Account Executive - Pharmacy Benefits
jobs.description_html:
Who We Are:

SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company.  Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service.  With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country.

We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values:

  • Integrity: Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new.
  • Courage: We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward—always.
  • Together: The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise.

Job Summary:

The Customer Success Team is focused on helping SmithRx’s clients derive the full value of their PBM services. We build and manage effective relationships with our customers’ operational leadership, communicating the value of our services in the context of customers’ business goals with the goal of retaining high performing, satisfied customers. We identify risks to client satisfaction proactively and collaborate across product and operational lines to tenaciously pursue solutions and advocate for our clients.

As a SmithRx Account Executive, you will be the primary strategic partner for our clients (employers, health plans, or TPA groups). You aren't just a "point of contact"; you are a healthcare consultant responsible for managing a book of business, driving client retention, and identifying opportunities to optimize pharmacy spend while improving member outcomes. You will bring strong industry and PBM knowledge and serve as a trusted advisor and business partner for your client’s operational leadership.

What you will do:

  • Establish and maintain relationships for large complex accounts
  • Own and facilitate end to end renewal process
  • Accountable for client satisfaction
  • Lead internal teams and act as internal client advocate
  • Provide executive updates on client status and risks.
  • Represent Customer Success in Finalist meetings.
  • Analyze pharmacy claims data to identify trends, provide cost-containment recommendations, and deliver quarterly/annual business reviews (QBRs).
  • Create and maintain a client strategic action plan.
  • Partner with clinical pharmacists to present formulary changes and clinical program recommendations to clients.
  • Stay ahead of industry trends, including drug pipelines, legislative changes, and competitive PBM landscapes.
  • Partner with leadership to review deliverables (QBR’s, reporting and client communications) to ensure "executive-ready" quality.
  • Coordinate with internal teams (Implementation, Operations, and Pricing) to resolve member issues and ensure seamless service delivery.
  • Serve as a formal or informal mentor to Account Managers (AMs), Account Specialists, and Account Coordinators; provide guidance on client communication strategies, career development, and navigating complex PBM workflows.
  • Responsible for understanding the Client's organization & structure, knowing the Client's product/services and staying aware of Client news and changes. Maintain and update Client record with changes. 
  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships in liaison role with Pharmacy Operations, service partner contacts and client contacts.
  • Ensure full, proactive communication of all important client account activities with cross-functional partners
  • Prioritize issues and assess escalations that may lead to client attrition risk with the Account Managers to ensure a strong mitigation plan is in place
  • Travel required: Up to 25%

What you will bring to SmithRx:

  • Requires 3-5 years of Account Executive experience in PBM or health insurance 
  • Requires 5+ years of direct account management or relationships management experience in the healthcare space; working knowledge of commercial health insurance and pharmacy benefits strongly preferred
  • Ability to interpret complex data sets (claims, rebates, and ROI) and translate them into actionable stories for C-suite executives.
  • A positive growth mindset with the ability to approach difficult situations in a calm and focused manner; understand the challenge and move forward tactfully towards a solution
  • Executive-level communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively navigate and mediate conflict and foster honest dialogue
  • Experience in Client relationship management ensuring expectations and deliverables are documented and met, key stakeholders are informed, and client satisfaction is achieved
  • Ability to work independently as well as part of an extended, cross-functional team
  • Self-driven, results-oriented and disciplined work ethic
  • Ability to take initiative with little to no direction
  • Be transparent and honest in a positive, professional and polite manner
  • Expert conflict resolution skills
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required

What SmithRx Offers You: 

  • Highly competitive wellness benefits including Medical, Pharmacy, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance and AD&D Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Benefits 
  • 401(k) Retirement Savings Program 
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Discretionary Paid Time Off

  • Well-stocked kitchen in office locations

Pharmacy Technicians in our Patient Care Center of Excellence may hold multiple duties to ensure ExactCare’s patients receive quality care out of their pharmacy services. They will work in a closed-door pharmacy environment, spending their time speaking with patients, doctors and facilities on the phone in addition to the outline job duties and responsibilities.

Job duties will vary from phone work and navigating multiple pharmacy software systems to supporting the various stages of patient care/contact. These areas of responsibility will fluctuate based on organizational needs, allowing the Pharmacy Technician to develop multiple skillsets.

jobs.title: Pharmacy Programs Specialist
jobs.description_html:
At Clover Health, we are committed to providing high-quality, affordable, and easy-to-understand healthcare plans for America’s seniors. We prioritize preventive care while leveraging data and technology through the Clover Assistant, a powerful tool that helps physicians make informed health recommendations. By giving doctors a holistic view of each member’s complete health history, we ensure better care at a lower cost—delivering the highest value to those who need it most.

The Clinical Pharmacy team is an innovative team that utilizes a member-centric approach to provide comprehensive medication management services. The Pharmacy Programs Specialist will work to support Medicare quality metrics, medication management initiatives, and maintain Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services compliance standards.

In this role, you would perform validation of claim adjudication ensuring appropriate access to care and support telephonic outreach for plan members, providers and other healthcare professionals. In addition, document activity and maintain electronic medical records while providing the highest quality healthcare and service to plan members and other internal and external partners.

As a Pharmacy Programs Specialist you will:

  • Create, manage, and respond to cases and/or escalate to Clinical Pharmacists on the Team.
  • Contribute to improving Part D Star measures by resolving root causes of medication management problems and taking appropriate action to provide recommendations based on profile review or patient interview.
  • Represent for the Pharmacy team and participate in cross-functional team meetings
  • Collect and present data and trends from Pharmacy Benefits Manager (PBM) delegated functions to cross-functional operational workgroups to propose process improvements
  • Deliver on cross-functional team initiatives and ad-hoc projects that impact Clover business goals
  • Provide guidance to internal and external teams in regards to pharmacy clinical and regulatory workflows, policies and processes
  • Serve as a liaison between PBM Account Management Team and Clover Health and escalate any questions that need PBM involvement for resolution.
  • Organize pharmacy team meetings with internal and external partners.
  • Think critically and problem solve to prioritize and work more efficiently
  • Improve team’s capacity and knowledge
  • Distribute work to peers and strategize completion of quality assurance projects that require short turn around times 
  • Provide recommendations on and deliver Part D content knowledge updates on internal knowledge base directory annually and ad-hoc 
  • Lead educational training for cross functional teams on Part D knowledge and vendor platforms
  • Participate in call center quality assurance reviews 
  • Perform strategic work to increase MTMP Star measure
  • Navigate and use tools and platforms required for task/queue-based work
  • Show curiosity as to how work impacts the business and how that work is generated
  • Complete a larger volume of assigned tasks with increasing focus on program/project-based opportunities and work and serve as a resource to others
  • Communicate with the pharmacy leadership team in a timely manner when issues arise.
  • File, review, and validate reports to ensure compliance with Medicare guidelines.
  • Gather data and generate reports to improve clinical pharmacy quality metrics.
  • Participate in training and orientation of new team members, as needed.
  • Execute other job duties as assigned.

Success in this role looks like:

  • Within 90 days: You have seamlessly integrated into the Pharmacy team and completed all the necessary training modules, familiarize yourself with the organization's platforms, and established a strong knowledge of Clover Health Part D benefit. You are capable of validating claim adjudication to ensure appropriate access to care and provide telephone support to plan members, prescribers, and pharmacies.
  • Within 6 months: You will be fully engaged in oversight of accurate Part D benefits that are in compliance with CMS requirements. You have demonstrated the ability to collaborate effectively with interdisciplinary teams, providing member experience support and contributing to resolving member medication related escalations.
  • Long-term: You will be measured based on pharmacy operational metrics, the integration of innovative technologies to enhance pharmacy services and improve patient outcomes, the enhancement of operational efficiency, and contributions to achieving the organization’s strategic objectives and key results.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have a National Certification (CPhT) Pharmacy Technician License (preferred).
  • You have at least three (3) years of experience working in pharmacy, managed care organization, medical office or in a hospital setting.
  • You are fluent in English and Spanish, both orally and in writing.
  • You have an understanding of managed care.
  • You have PC skills in Windows-based applications.
  • You have excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • You are able to work Eastern Time (ET) hours; candidates in this time zone, preferred.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location. 
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses

jobs.title: Project Manager, Healthcare and Pharmaceutical Advertising
jobs.description_html:
When you join Precision AQ, you become part of a team united by a shared purpose: helping healthcare innovations reach the patients who need them most. Our work supports the launch of new treatments, advances scientific communication, and helps clients navigate complex healthcare challenges. We believe our best work comes from collaboration, diverse perspectives, and a culture where great ideas can come from anyone. 

At Precision AQ, success is built on teamwork. We value people who are curious, accountable, and committed to supporting those around them. Our culture is grounded in collaboration, mutual respect, and a shared drive to deliver exceptional results for our clients. Here, you'll work alongside talented colleagues who challenge and inspire one another while making a meaningful impact across healthcare. 

The Project Management team is at the center of agency operations, connecting people, processes, and priorities to keep work moving forward. We are strategic problem solvers and trusted partners who collaborate across functions to deliver high-quality work on time and within budget. 

As a Project Manager, you will lead projects from planning through execution, partnering closely with account, creative, editorial, and production teams to ensure successful delivery. You'll play a critical role in balancing timelines, resources, budgets, and stakeholder expectations while helping teams navigate challenges and maintain momentum. This is an opportunity to work in a highly collaborative environment, contribute to a wide range of healthcare and pharmaceutical initiatives, and make a measurable impact on client success. 

About You 

  • You are a proactive problem solver who enjoys bringing structure to complex projects and competing priorities. 
  • You are a strong communicator who can collaborate effectively with individuals across multiple functions and levels. 
  • You thrive in fast-paced environments and can adapt quickly when priorities shift. 
  • You are highly organized and detail-oriented, with a commitment to delivering quality work on time and within budget. 
  • You enjoy leading meetings, driving accountability, and keeping teams aligned around shared goals. 
  • You take a solutions-oriented approach and can identify risks, evaluate options, and keep projects moving forward. 

About the Role 

Reporting to senior project management leadership, you will support the planning, execution, and delivery of client programs and projects. You will develop project plans, timelines, and workflows while partnering closely with account teams and other stakeholders to ensure alignment on objectives, budgets, and deliverables. You will facilitate internal meetings, manage project status communications, and oversee workflow processes from kickoff through final delivery. Additionally, you will monitor project progress, identify potential risks, and help keep projects on track. 

Required Experience 

  • Bachelor's degree required. 
  • Minimum of 2 years of project management experience, including project planning, execution, and delivery. 
  • Experience managing multiple projects, timelines, and stakeholders simultaneously. 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management software or workflow management tools. 
  • Strong meeting facilitation, communication, and organizational skills. 
  • Ability to identify risks, manage priorities, and drive projects to completion. 

Helpful Experience 

  • Advertising agency experience. 
  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical or healthcare clients. 
  • Familiarity with digital, print, and broadcast production processes. 
  • Experience working within cross-functional client service environments.

jobs.title: SVP, Pharmacy Relations
jobs.description_html:
We are a healthcare technology company that provides platforms and solutions to improve the management and access of cost-effective pharmacy benefits. Our technology helps enterprise and partnership clients simplify their businesses and helps consumers save on prescriptions.

As a leader in SaaS technology for healthcare, we offer innovative solutions with integrated intelligence on a single enterprise platform that connects the pharmacy ecosystem.  With our expertise and modern, modular platform, our partners use real-time data to transform their business performance and optimize their innovative models in the marketplace.

Position summary

The SVP of Pharmacy Relations sets the standard for how RxSense engages, retains, and grows its pharmacy relationships and brings consistency to how RxSense discount card brands and account managers serve our pharmacy clients. This role is responsible for partner retention, satisfaction, and organic growth across RxSense's portfolio of pharmacy relationships, and all facets of retail, mail and specialty contracting across all business segments (cash and funded).

You will lead a small team of account and relationship managers and partner closely with the pricing, contracting, and reconciliation teams who will continue to own those functions, so the SVP can focus on the relationship, the strategy, and the growth opportunity. This is a highly visible role with regular exposure to RxSense executive leadership and to senior leaders throughout the retail pharmacy industry.

Key responsibilities

Proactive account management

  • Implement an engagement model with a proactive cadence of business reviews, strategic check-ins, and performance reporting for each assigned pharmacy partner.
  • Build and maintain trusted, senior-level relationships with pharmacy partner stakeholders, serving as their primary advocate inside RxSense.

 

Strategic alignment

  • Develop deep insight into each partner's business, market position, and long-term objectives, and ensure RxSense's engagement plan is aligned to them.
  • Bring consistency across account managers, pharmacy clients, and RxSense brands (including SingleCare, ParamountRx, and Integris), so partners experience one coordinated RxSense rather than separate teams.

Growth and opportunity identification

  • Aggressively and proactively promote the full RxSense solution set, including digital marketplace, GlobalBIN, brand affordability programs, and pricing sophistication, to address retail pharmacy challenges.
  • Identify and pursue organic growth opportunities within existing accounts and clearly communicate the value RxSense already delivers so it is recognized and rewarded.

Team leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of account and relationship managers, standardizing practices, tools, and reporting across the portfolio.

Feedback and innovation loop

  • Establish a structured feedback loop from pharmacy partners back into RxSense's product and technology teams to inform new solutions.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, Operations, Underwriting and the pricing and contracting teams to deliver a seamless partner experience end to end.

What success looks like

A consistent and scalable engagement model in place across all assigned pharmacy partners.

Documented account plans and a regular business review cadence for every partner.

A high-functioning Pharmacy Relations team with clear roles, coaching, and standardized reporting.

At least one organic growth or expansion opportunity identified and advanced per major partner.

A working feedback channel from partners into RxSense's product roadmap.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; PharmD or MBA preferred.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in account management, client success, or partner relationship roles, ideally spanning retail pharmacy, pharmacy benefits, or a related healthcare setting.
  • Experience within a retail pharmacy chain or pharmacy operations environment strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated success building or leading a client success or account management team, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.
  • Track record of driving retention and organic growth within existing enterprise accounts.
  • Strong executive presence, with the ability to build credibility and trust with senior pharmacy stakeholders.
  • Solid understanding of the pharmacy benefits and retail pharmacy landscape, including the competitive and reimbursement pressures partners face.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the judgment to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder relationships.

RxSense believes that a diverse workforce is a more talented and productive workforce. As such, we are an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. Our recruitment process is free from discriminatory hiring practices and all qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, age, or national origin.  Neither will qualified applicants be discriminated against on the basis of disability or protected veteran status.  We believe in the strength of the collaboration, creativity and sense of community a diverse workforce brings.

jobs.title: Community Pharmacy Team Lead (Thursday to Monday, 10:00AM - 6:30PM ET)
jobs.description_html:
AnewHealth is one of the nation’s leading pharmacy care management companies that specializes in caring for people with the most complex, chronic needs—wherever they call home. We enable better outcomes for patients and the healthcare organizations who support them. Established in 2023 through the combination of ExactCare and Tabula Rasa HealthCare, we provide a suite of solutions that includes comprehensive pharmacy services; full-service pharmacy benefit management; and specialized support services for Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. With over 1,400 team members, we care for more than 100,000 people across all 50 states.

Job Details

The Community Pharmacy Team Lead supports the Community Pharmacy Team Manager by supervising a team of pharmacists and technicians responsible for patient care, medication dispensing support, pharmacy operations, clinical documentation, quality assurance, and client service activities.

This role serves as a first-line resource for staff, helping coordinate daily workflow, resolve operational and clinical escalations, support adherence to standard operating procedures, and ensure timely, accurate, and compliant pharmacy services. The Team Lead uses clinical judgment, operational knowledge, and strong communication skills to help the team deliver safe, efficient, patient-centered medication management services.

The Team Lead is expected to model professionalism, accountability, sound decision-making, and collaboration across pharmacists, technicians, managers, clients, prescribers, community pharmacies, and other healthcare partners.

Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Daily Workflow Oversight

  • Provides day-to-day guidance, support, and directions to assigned pharmacists and technicians.

  • Assists the Community Pharmacy Team Manager with monitoring daily workflow, staffing alignment, work queues, service levels, and completion of assigned tasks.

  • Serves as a first point of escalation for staff questions related to workflow, patient care processes, documentation, dispensing support, and client-specific procedures.

  • Help prioritize urgent, same-day, next-business-day, cycle-fill, and other operational requests based on patient needs, regulatory requirements, and company procedures.

  • Supports staff in resolving barriers that may delay medication access, documentation completion, prescription processing, or patient care follow-up.

  • Monitors team productivity, quality, and timeliness and communicates concerns, trends, or improvement opportunities to the Community Pharmacy Team Manager.

  • Assists with onboarding, training, coaching, and ongoing development of pharmacists and technicians.

  • Reinforces standard operating procedures, client-specific workflows, documentation standards, quality expectations, and compliance requirements.

  • Helps maintain a positive, accountable, and collaborative team culture.

  • Escalates performance, attendance, conduct, quality, or compliance concerns to the Community Pharmacy Team Manager in a timely and objective manner.

  • Ensures clinical recommendation standards and documentation quality; leads calibration and coaching.

ATM/CPN/Same-Day Medication Support

  • Monitors Same Day Technician Pre-Check & Pharmacist Verification queues to ensure compliance with client SLAs.

  • Supports oversight of ATM dispensing and related operational activities.

  • Assists with Community Pharmacy Network transfers and ensures appropriate internal documentation of completed work.

  • Help coordinate medication procurement through local pharmacies for same-day or urgent medication needs.

  • Provides or verifies necessary prescription documentation to support safe and accurate dispensing by local pharmacies.

  • Supports staff in providing appropriate billing, insurance, and processing information to community pharmacy partners when needed.

  • Helps identify and resolve CPN-related issues, including technology, logistics, documentation, workflow, billing, and communication concerns.

  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with community pharmacy partners.

  • Assists with training staff and clients on proper CPN and same-day medication procedures.

Patient Pharmacotherapy and Clinical Support

  • Supports the team in maintaining accurate patient-specific medication profiles and care documentation within company systems.

  • Reviews medication-related questions and escalations from pharmacists, technicians, clients, prescribers, patients, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.

  • Uses professional judgment to help ensure timely, accurate, and appropriate pharmaceutical care.

  • Reviews new medication requests, medication changes, and patient-specific clinical information when needed to support safety, appropriateness, and continuity of care.

  • Assists pharmacists with identifying medication-related problems and developing appropriate recommendations to improve patient outcomes and reduce medication-related risk.

  • Supports monthly medication profile review, cycle-fill review, medication review preparation, and other patient care activities as assigned.

  • Helps ensure that patient care decisions, interventions, communications, and follow-up actions are documented accurately and consistently.

  • Provides medication counseling, education, and clinical clarification when appropriate and within scope of practice.

  • Supports prospective drug utilization review and other pharmacist responsibilities as required by applicable laws, regulations, and company policy.

  • Participates in on-call, emergency call retrieval, or after-hours support when assigned.

Quality Assurance, Compliance, and Continuous Improvement

  • Assists the Community Pharmacy Team Manager with monitoring team compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, quality standards, and pharmacy practice expectations.

  • Reviews workflow trends, documentation quality, dispensing support issues, client concerns, and operational barriers to identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Supports investigation, documentation, and resolution of quality assurance events, HIPAA concerns, fraud, waste, and abuse concerns, medication access issues, or other compliance matters.

  • Helps ensure that patient care activities, coding, billing, dispensing support, and operational actions are properly documented in company systems.

  • Provides reports, feedback, and analysis to the Community Pharmacy Team Manager as requested.

  • Collaborates with operations, clinical leadership, account management, IT, software development, fulfillment, and other internal partners to improve workflow, automation, quality, and efficiency.

  • Participates in process improvement initiatives, staff education, workflow redesign, and implementation of new procedures or technology.

  • Supports a culture of continuous audit readiness and proactive issue resolution.

Communication and Cross-Functional Communication

  • Serves as a professional and responsive resource for pharmacists, technicians, clients, prescribers, patients, caregivers, community pharmacies, and internal departments.

  • Communicates clearly and respectfully through written, verbal, and interpersonal interactions.

  • Help ensure that staff communications are accurate, timely, complete, and aligned with company expectations.

  • Partners with the Community Pharmacy Team Manager to identify recurring client concerns, service gaps, workflow breakdowns, and staff training needs.

  • Escalates urgent or high-risk matters promptly and appropriately.

  • Promote collaboration between pharmacists and technicians to support safe, efficient, and patient-centered pharmacy care.

  • Embody AnewHealth’s Core Values in all communications and interactions.

  • Other duties as assigned.

The above essential functions are representative of major duties of positions in this job classification. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs. Other duties may be assigned similar to the above consistent with knowledge, skills and abilities required for the job.  Not all of the duties may be assigned to a position.

Qualifications: These represent the desired qualifications of the ideal candidate. They are not meant to limit consideration for candidates who do not meet all of the standards listed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education

  • PharmD, required

  • BCGP, required

  • A current, active license in the state of NJ, required.

  • Must be registered or eligible to become registered with the appropriate State Board of Pharmacy within 90 days of hire. 

Experience

  • Required: 1+ years of pharmacy operations, clinical pharmacy, geriatric pharmacy, PACE, long-term care, community pharmacy, or related healthcare experience. 

  • Prior experience providing day-to-day team guidance, workflow coordination, training, mentoring, or informal leadership. 

  • Experience working in a call center, centralized pharmacy, clinical operations, medication management, or high-volume pharmacy environment. 

  • Experience with quality assurance, documentation review, performance improvement, and staff coaching. 

  • Experience supporting geriatric patients, medically complex populations, or interdisciplinary care teams. 

  • Experience with internal pharmacy systems, EHR platforms, pharmacy dispensing systems, clinical decision support tools, and Microsoft Office Suite. 

Skills & Abilities

  • Proficient with MS Office Suite.  

  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written. 

  • Ability to communicate effectively and professionally through written, verbal (e.g., face-to-face, telephonically and/or virtual communication platforms), and interpersonal skills as applied when interacting with employees, patients, healthcare professionals, clients, or agency representatives; successfully conveying and exchanging information at an appropriate level and in a positive and timely manner.

  • Strong technical and computer skills to navigate proprietary and other pharmacy software and the initiative to propose suggestions to improve operations and proprietary system development and enhancements.

  • Demonstrated experience with problem-solving, conflict resolution, and project management skills.

  • Detail oriented and organized with the ability to work with a sense of urgency, work under pressure, multi-task, and achieve deadlines without sacrificing quality. 

  • Strong data entry capability. 

  • Strong analytical skills with good clinical judgement and decision-making including (1) the ability to effectively and efficiently identify and rectify medication-related problems, and (2) assess patients using verbal and/or visual cues, when appropriate.

  • Knowledge of state and federal laws and regulations, including HIPAA and Fraud, Waste, and Abuse. 

  • Possesses high level of integrity

  • Quality-oriented

  • Innovative

  • Steadfast

This is a full-time position with an expectation to work an average of 40 hours per week and be available outside of normal business hours to meet customer expectations on an ad-hoc basis. Schedules are set to accommodate the requirements of the position and the needs of the organization and may be adjusted as needed. Rotating weekly On-Call oversight schedule required.

This is a remote position.

AnewHealth offers a comprehensive benefit package for full-time employees that includes medical/dental/vision, flexible spending, company-paid life insurance and short-term disability as well as voluntary benefits, 401(k), Paid Time Off and paid holidays. Medical, dental and vision coverage are effective 1st of the month following date of hire.

jobs.title: Pharmacovigilance Physician
jobs.description_html:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Environmental Conditions

Office

Job Description

Join Us as a Pharmacovigilance Physician – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation

At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life - enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while taking science a step beyond through research, development and delivery of life-changing therapies. With clinical trials conducted in 100+ countries and ongoing development of novel frameworks for clinical research through our PPD clinical research portfolio, our work spans laboratory, digital and decentralized clinical trial services. Your determination to deliver quality and accuracy will improve health outcomes that people and communities depend on – now and in the future.

The Pharmacovigilance Physician provides medical oversight of pharmacovigilance activities to ensure company SOPs, client directives, good clinical practice, and regulatory requirements are followed. Attends and presents at sponsor meetings, provides medical and pharmacovigilance consultation to clients and project team members. May also support business development activities. Provides medical review and analysis for clinical trial serious adverse events, marketed products ICSR with focus on triage, seriousness, expectedness, causality assessment, appropriate selection of adverse event terms using MedDRA terminology, narrative review and periodic safety reports (e.g. PBRER, PSUR, DSUR) as well as other client deliverables (e.g. labeling reconciliation documents, CTD modules, REMS, RMP, and CSR). Identifies and investigates safety signals and contributes to the management of the benefit-risk profile of assigned products.

We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years.

What You'll Do:
• Manage all medical aspects of contracted pharmacovigilance tasks across the pharmaceutical product life cycle.
• Adhere to applicable regulations and ICH guidelines regarding clinical trials, regulatory documents, and safety issues, as well as client SOPs/directives, project-specific WPDs for assigned projects, and the organization’s corporate policies and SOPs/WPDs.
• Provide medical consultation to team members and communicate clearly with associates and clients, maintaining an open line of communication to ensure all procedures are followed appropriately.
• Provide therapeutic and protocol training on assigned studies, as requested.
• Assist in writing (interpretation of safety data) and/or reviewing the safety portion of the CSR, IND/NDA report, ICSR, signal detection reports, periodic reports, RMP, REMS, CTD modules; scientifically review aggregate reports, contribute to label updates, review and assess literature, and support dossier maintenance and risk management activities to ensure that the medical content is accurate and complete.
• Provide medical review of cases and perform reviews of adverse events of special interest and serious adverse events.
• Perform data reviews as specified in the client contract and data validation manual, including review of coding listings and/or full safety data to assess potential safety concerns. Medically review adverse event and serious adverse event data from all sources (solicited, spontaneous, literature, etc.) as contracted.

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • Must be MD or equivalent or MBBS qualified graduate
  • 5+ Years of experience in pharmaceutical/biotech industry with at least 2 years in pharmacovigilance/drug safety (global experience is a plus)

jobs.title: Staff Pharmacist, North Carolina
jobs.description_html:
Company Overview:

Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.  Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients. 

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock. 

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

Hours: Full-time, salaried (40hrs/week), Mon-Fri, 7:30am-9pm ET rotating shifts and rotating Saturdays 7:00am-5pm ET

The Opportunity:

As a BlinkRx Pharmacist, you are the clinical backbone of our closed-door facility. You will verify prescriptions with speed and precision, provide proactive phone-based patient counseling, and collaborate with prescribers to keep medications moving without compromising safety. This role is ideal for pharmacists who thrive in a structured, high-throughput environment and are passionate about improving patient outcomes at scale. 

Responsibilities:

Prescription Verification and Dispensing

  • Review and clinically verify new and refill prescriptions for therapeutic appropriateness, drug-drug interactions, contraindications, and dosing accuracy
  • Validate prescription data entry performed by pharmacy technicians, ensuring transcription accuracy from provider orders and transfer records
  • Perform pharmacist verification of filled prescriptions in a closed-door fulfillment environment, confirming accuracy of drug, dose, quantity, NDC, and labeling prior to release for shipment   
  • Perform daily prospective drug utilization review (DUR) to identify and resolve clinical flags before fulfillment
  • Manage specialty medication handling requirements including cold-chain verification

Patient Care

All patient interaction at BlinkRx is conducted by phone or digital platforms. Our pharmacists are the primary clinical contact for patients and must deliver a high standard of care in every call.

  • Provide proactive outbound patient counseling calls for new prescriptions, addressing drug education, expected side effects, dosing instructions, storage requirements, and adherence strategies
  • Handle inbound clinical patient calls related to counseling and clinical inquiries, while directing non-clinical inquiries, such as refill status and delivery questions, to the patient support team.
  • Document all patient interactions thoroughly in the patient profile within the pharmacy management system
  • Support Spanish-speaking patients with bilingual counseling where applicable

Prescriber Collaboration and Clinical Outreach

  • Contact prescriber offices via phone and electronic messaging to clarify incomplete, ambiguous, or clinically inappropriate prescriptions prior to dispensing
  • Partner with prescribers on therapeutic substitutions, DAW overrides, and formulary alternatives to reduce dispensing delays

Pharmacy Technician Supervision and Workflow Management

  • Supervise pharmacy technicians across data entry, prescription processing, packaging, and fulfillment workflows in accordance with state board regulations and in collaboration with technician management
  • Conduct real-time quality checks on technician work product, providing immediate corrective feedback to maintain accuracy standards
  • Identify and escalate technician performance trends to pharmacy leadership; participate in coaching and training as directed

Compliance, Safety and Quality

  • Ensure strict compliance with HIPAA, state pharmacy practice acts, federal DEA regulations, and all BlinkRx corporate policies
  • Oversee proper handling, documentation, and destruction of PHI-containing records and materials in alignment with privacy protocols
  • Participate in quality assurance activities including internal audits, prescription error tracking, and near-miss reporting
  • Report adverse drug events and medication errors through established pharmacovigilance channels, when applicable
  • Maintain fulfillment area compliance standards, including proper storage of temperature-sensitive medications

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with pharmacy leadership, patient services, clinical, compliance, and technology teams to drive operational and clinical improvements
  • Coordinate with the shipping and fulfillment team to resolve packaging errors, return-to-sender issues, and delivery failures affecting patient medication access
  • Provide clinical input on technology enhancements, workflow tools, and software configurations that affect the pharmacist verification or patient counseling experience
  • Participate in team huddles, quality reviews, and department meetings to support continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications:

Required

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree from an ACPE-accredited College of Pharmacy
  • Active Missouri Pharmacy License in good standing with the Missouri Board of Pharmacy
  • Strong command of the English language (written and verbal); bilingual Spanish preferred for phone-based patient counseling
  • Demonstrated ability to perform high-volume prescription verification with strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Strong technical aptitude and ability to learn pharmacy management systems, verification platforms, and internal workflow tools

Preferred

  • 3+ years of experience in a mail order, specialty, retail or closed-door fulfillment pharmacy
  • Active pharmacy licensure required in home state; candidates must obtain licensure in 3 additional states from the list below within the first 9 months of hire (prior licensure in any of the following states is a plus):
    • AK, AL, AR, CA, ID, IL, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MS, NE, NV, OK, OR, TN, TX, VA, WV
  • Familiarity with pharmacovigilance or adverse drug event reporting protocols

What Success Looks Like:

  • Prescription verification queues are processed accurately and on time without sacrificing clinical quality
  • Every patient who receives a counseling call feels informed, supported, and confident in their therapy 
  • Prescriber outreach is proactive and efficient, minimizing dispensing delays caused by incomplete or unclear orders
  • Compliance and quality standards are upheld without exception in a fast-paced environment
  • You are a trusted clinical partner within the BlinkRx team — shaping the patient experience from behind the scenes

 #blinkindeed

Why Join Us:

It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year.  Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Applicants who provide their phone number and consent to receive text messages may receive SMS or MMS updates from Blink Health regarding their application.

jobs.title: Sr. Pharmacy Performance & Operations Specialist
jobs.description_html:
Government Employees Health Association, Inc. (G.E.H.A) is a nonprofit member association that provides health and dental benefits that millions of federal employees and retirees, military retirees and their families have counted on since 1937. Offering one of the largest health and dental benefit provider networks available to federal employees in the United States, G.E.H.A empowers health and wellness by meeting its members where they are, when they need care.

 

G.E.H.A has one mission: To empower federal workers to be healthy and well.

The Sr. Pharmacy Performance & Operations Specialist is responsible for oversight, performance management, and operational execution of G.E.H.A’s FEHB and PSHB pharmacy programs. This role owns PBM performance monitoring, contractual compliance, and operational integrity, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and enterprise objectives. The position serves as a subject matter expert and primary liaison to the PBM, driving issue resolution, enforcing contractual obligations, and delivering data-driven insights to inform strategic decisions and optimize member outcomes.

SKILLS

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Oversee PBM contract performance, ensuring alignment with contractual guarantees and federal program requirements.
  • Prepare, validate, and submit annual pharmacy benefit changes for FEHB and PSHB programs.
  • Develop division reports, dashboards, and executive-level presentation materials to monitor plan performance.
  • Manage PBM contractual credits, including reporting, validation, and quality assurance processes.
  • Monitor and enforce compliance with PBM contractual obligations and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for pharmacy benefits, including commercial benefit design and configuration.
  • Draft, review, and coordinate PBM performance-related penalty letters and enforcement actions.
  • Support contract governance activities, including performance reviews, issue escalation, and resolution tracking.
  • Monitor call center performance metrics, identify trends, and drive solutions to improve member experience.
  • Track eligibility changes and population shifts, assessing impact on pharmacy benefit performance and operations.
  • Identify contractual or operational gaps and develop corrective action plans to address shortfalls.
  • Review pharmacy-related Customer Success content to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with benefits.
  • Respond to internal and external audit inquiries, providing documentation and ensuring audit readiness.
  • Validate production and pre-production claims accuracy, ensuring alignment with benefit design and contract terms.
  • Investigate and resolve complex pharmacy-related member issues and escalations.
  • Manage day-to-day pharmacy program operations, including implementation and administration of new initiatives.
  • Serve as the primary liaison to the PBM for operational issues, program implementation, and eligibility matters.
  • Coordinate cross-functional efforts with internal stakeholders to resolve PBM-related issues and drive performance improvement.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support pharmacy program performance and operational objectives.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, Pharmacy, Business Administration, Public Health, or related field.
  • A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in pharmacy operations, pharmacy benefit management (PBM), health plan operations, or federal health program administration (e.g., FEHB, PSHB)
  • FEHB/PSHB program knowledge: Familiarity with federal pharmacy benefit requirements and regulatory expectations.
  • Analytical and reporting skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and ability to build dashboards, analyze trends, and interpret performance data.
  • Contract interpretation: Skilled in understanding and applying contractual terms to operational scenarios.
  • Problem-solving abilities: Capable of diagnosing issues, identifying root causes, and developing solutions.
  • Communication skills: Able to explain complex pharmacy concepts and decisions.
  • Attention to detail: Strong accuracy in reviewing claims, reports, and compliance documentation.
  • Cross functional collaboration: Ability to work with internal teams, PBM partners, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Executive communication: ability to translate complex PBM, financial, and regulatory concepts into clear, actionable insights.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced pharmacy, healthcare, or business administration degree (e.g., MPH, MHA, MBA,  PharmD).
  • Data visualization tools: Experience with Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.
  • Project management certification: PMP, CAPM, or equivalent.
  • Regulatory compliance experience: Familiarity with OPM, CMS, or other federal oversight bodies.
  • Process improvement training: Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies.

Work-at-home requirements

  • Must have the ability to provide a non-cellular High Speed Internet Service such as Fiber, DSL, or cable Modems for a home office.

  • A minimum standard speed for optimal performance of 30x5 (30mpbs download x 5mpbs upload) is required.

  • Latency (ping) response time lower than 80 ms

  • Hotspots, satellite and wireless internet service is NOT allowed for this role.

  • A dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information

How we value you

  • Competitive pay/salary ranges

  • Incentive plan

  • Health/Vision/Dental benefits effective day one

  • 401(k) retirement plan:  company match – dollar for dollar up to 4% employee contribution (pretax or Roth options) plus a 6% annual company contribution   

  • Robust employee well-being program

  • Paid Time Off

  • Personal Community Enrichment Time

  • Company-provided Basic Life and AD&D

  • Company-provided Short-Term & Long-Term Disability

  • Tuition Assistance Program

While this is a remote opportunity, at this time G.E.H.A does not hire employees from U.S. territories or the following states: Alaska, Hawaii, California, Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, New York, Connecticut, Vermont, Pennsylvania, Maine.

Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only.  G.E.H.A considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as, market and business considerations when extending an offer.

The target hiring range for this position is $81,672 - $103,320 USD. At G.E.H.A, the current maximum salary for this role is $115,128 USD. While initial compensation may vary based on experience and qualifications, there is a path to work toward this top rate through performance and continued growth within the organization.

G.E.H.A is an Equal Opportunity Employer, which means we will not discriminate against any individual based on sex, race, color, national origin, disability, religion, age, military status, genetic information, veteran status, pregnancy, marital status, gender identity, and sexual orientation, as well as all other characteristics and qualities protected by federal, state, or local law. G.E.H.A will not discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their compensation or the compensation of another employee or applicant. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

G.E.H.A is headquartered in Lee's Summit, Missouri, in the Kansas City area. We recognize the importance of balance and flexibility and offer hybrid and work-from-home options for many of our roles.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA or Remote or Hybrid
jobs.description_html:
About us:

Braveheart Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and other serious cardiovascular diseases. Our lead product candidate, BHB-1893, is a next-generation oral small-molecule cardiac myosin inhibitor (CMI) being developed for the treatment of obstructive HCM (oHCM) and non-obstructive HCM (nHCM). Braveheart’s goal is to improve the treatment options for these patients by enhancing speed of onset, depth of gradient response, systolic safety, reversibility and reducing prescribing complexity.

With a proven leadership team, a strong financial foundation, and a high-value late-stage asset, Braveheart Bio represents an outstanding opportunity for ambitious, mission-driven professionals to make a tangible impact in a high-profile and rapidly evolving therapeutic area.

 

The role:

The Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance (PV) will serve as a key leader within Braveheart Bio's Drug Safety and Pharmacovigilance organization, partnering closely with the Vice President, Drug Safety and Pharmacovigilance to execute the company's global drug safety and pharmacovigilance strategy and ensure excellence in pharmacovigilance operations, safety surveillance, signal management, aggregate reporting, vendor oversight, and regulatory compliance.

This role will play a critical part in preparing the organization for global Phase 3 execution, regulatory submissions, and eventual commercialization. The Senior Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for safety surveillance, signal detection and management, aggregate safety reporting, risk management, pharmacovigilance compliance, and outsourced PV operations. The role will also serve as the operational pharmacovigilance lead for Braveheart's global co-development partnership, ensuring effective safety governance, implementation and oversight of Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs) and Pharmacovigilance Agreements (PVAs), management of safety data exchange and reconciliation activities, and alignment of safety surveillance, aggregate reporting, and benefit-risk assessments across global development programs. In addition, this leader will help scale Braveheart's pharmacovigilance infrastructure, systems, processes, and operating model to support the organization's evolution from late-stage clinical development through regulatory approval and commercialization.

Key responsibilities:

  • Lead strategic and operational pharmacovigilance activities supporting Braveheart's development and future commercial portfolio.
  • Oversee all PV operations and compliance activities throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring adherence to global regulatory requirements and reporting timelines.
  • Build, scale, and continuously improve PV infrastructure, systems, processes, and oversight frameworks to support global Phase 3 programs and future commercialization.
  • Oversee ICSR collection, case review, processing, reconciliation, reporting, and associated quality activities.
  • Lead safety surveillance activities, including signal detection, evaluation, management, and communication of emerging safety risks.
  • Provide scientific and operational leadership for aggregate safety reporting activities, including DSURs, PBRERs/PSURs, IND Annual Reports, Investigator Brochures, and other safety deliverables.
  • Support development and implementation of Risk Management Plans (RMPs), REMS, Safety Management Plans, and other risk management activities.
  • Serve as the pharmacovigilance subject matter expert for regulatory submissions and health authority interactions, including preparation of safety sections and responses to regulatory queries.
  • Provide case review, analysis, and guidance during SAE case assessment, reporting, and safety issue escalation activities for Braveheart investigational products.
  • Contribute to safety sections of clinical and regulatory documents, including protocols, informed consent forms, investigator brochures, clinical study reports, integrated safety summaries, and marketing application submissions.
  • Serve as the operational pharmacovigilance lead for global co-development and licensing partnerships, including oversight of Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs), Pharmacovigilance Agreements (PVAs), safety governance activities, and partner safety data reconciliation.
